item.title: GovBrief Today #657
item.description: Pete Hegseth signed a military pact in Caracas today with the government American troops attacked 10 months ago. He called that attack “a day of liberation for Venezuela.” His host, acting President Delcy Rodríguez, was Nicolás Maduro’s vice president. Her term ran out in July and no election is scheduled. The pact promises training, intelligence, and equipment to an army led by Gen. Gustavo González López, who ran Maduro’s intelligence service. The United States sanctioned him in 2015 for human rights abuses. About 2,000 miles north, the administration asked the Supreme Court for the third time to let it deport hundreds of thousands of Venezuelans who once had legal protection to remain in the United States. Government lawyers warned that without a ruling by Friday, about 1,800 of them would have to be let out of immigration jails. On February 1, 2025, I typed a list of nine things I never imagined a government doing in one day and sent it to my family. I’ve sent one every night since: 9,996 stories over 657 straight nights, free and without ads. Add your email address at govbrief.today and I’ll send it to you too. NEW: Zoom In is now live!
